profile.headline: Engineering @ Crowdstrike
profile.summary:
I’m an experienced software engineer specializing in cloud technologies, embedded systems, and networking. With roles at AWS, Rubrik, and Gigamon, I’ve led projects that improve product performance, security, and innovation, with expertise in AWS, Azure, Kubernetes, and Broadcom technologies.
Beyond my skills, I am driven by curiosity and a desire to explore new challenges. I thrive in ambiguous environments and am always eager to step out of my comfort zone to learn and grow. Whether developing next-gen solutions or tackling new problems, I am committed to delivering high-impact results while continuously expanding my knowledge.

patents.title: Security Access for a Switch Device
patents.description: A method for providing user access to a network switch appliance, includes: receiving from a user a request to access configuration item for the network switch appliance, the network switch appliance configured to pass packets received from a network to network monitoring instruments; and determining, using a processing unit, whether to allow the user to access the configuration item for the network switch appliance based on information regarding the user.

patents.title: Filtration of network traffic using virtually-extended ternary content-addressable memory (TCAM)
patents.description: Ternary content-addressable memory (TCAM) of an ingress appliance in a visibility fabric may include rules for filtering traffic received by the ingress appliance. But the TCAM has limited space for rules and can become easily exhausted. By migrating rules to other visibility nodes in the visibility fabric, the techniques introduced here allow the TCAM to be virtually extended across multiple visibility nodes. More specifically, upon receiving a data packet at an ingress port, the ingress visibility node can tag the data packet with an identifier based on which ingress port received the data packet. The ingress visibility node can then determine, based on the identifier, whether the data packet should be filtered using a rule stored in the TCAM of the ingress visibility node or a rule stored in the TCAM of some visibility node in the visibility fabric.
